findings.finding: The answer says the tender will be submitted "before 29 January 2027". The RFP deadline is 22 Jan 2027 12:00 CET. A tender submitted after 22 January would be rejected.
findings.suggestion: Replace the date with the correct deadline (22 Jan 2027 12:00 CET) and plan the submission so it is in before then.

findings.finding: The answer lists "a Norwegian savings bank" as a reference. CAP-03 says a Norwegian reference is not yet available. The only references are a Swedish savings bank (live 2023) and a Danish regional bank (live 2025).
findings.suggestion: Remove the Norwegian reference. List only the Swedish and Danish banks, which still meet the requirement of two Nordic/EU/EEA references within five years.

findings.finding: The answer says "Partly met... nightly files" and gives no evidence. CAP-21 states that account events are published to an event streaming platform that other systems can subscribe to. The answer understates the capability and loses evaluation points.
findings.suggestion: Check with a specialist and align the answer with CAP-21. Cite CAP-21 as evidence.

findings.finding: The answer is empty for a shall-requirement (log all API calls, keep at least five years), and no specialist flag is set. CAP-34 supports logging of time, caller and consent reference, with configurable retention up to 10 years.
findings.suggestion: Draft an answer based on CAP-34 that explicitly covers the five-year retention, or flag it for a specialist.

findings.finding: The answer claims "full data lineage from every source system to the bank's reports". CAP-43 only covers lineage from source systems into the data platform, and states that lineage into the bank's own reporting tools is not included.
findings.suggestion: Change the answer to "Partly met". State that lineage covers source to data platform and that the last step into the bank's reporting tools is not included.

findings.finding: The answer says "support access stay within the EU/EEA". CAP-71 says third-line support uses a follow-the-sun model with an engineering team outside the EU/EEA, and EU/EEA-only support access is a paid option. Only CAP-70 (hosting and backups) is cited, so the support-access part is unsupported.
findings.suggestion: State that hosting and backups are in Norway and Finland. Disclose the non-EU/EEA third-line support and the paid EU/EEA-only option, citing CAP-71.

findings.finding: The answer says incidents are reported "within 24 hours of detection". The requirement is four hours, and CAP-74 says two hours. As written, the answer does not meet the requirement and contradicts the capability sheet.
findings.suggestion: Correct the answer to two hours from detection (CAP-74), which meets the four-hour requirement.

findings.finding: The answer says "Our standard SLA guarantees 99.95 %". CAP-80 says the standard SLA is 99.9 %, and 99.95 % is only in the Premium SLA at extra cost. The answer claims "Met" and leaves out the cost.
findings.suggestion: State that 99.95 % requires the Premium SLA and say that it carries an extra cost. Have the price section reflect this.

findings.finding: The answer says maintenance is done "between 01:00 and 05:00". CAP-81 says the standard window is 00:00–04:00. The 14-day notice is correct, but the time window does not match the sheet, so the claim is unsupported.
findings.suggestion: Check with a specialist whether the window can be moved to 01:00–05:00. If not, state "Partly met" and give the actual window.

findings.finding: The answer says "24/7 support in English and Norwegian". CAP-82 says 24/7 support is in English only, and Norwegian-speaking support is weekdays 08:00–16:00. The requirement is 24/7 in both languages for critical incidents.
findings.suggestion: Change the answer to "Partly met". Describe 24/7 English support and Norwegian support on weekdays 08:00–16:00, or check with a specialist whether 24/7 Norwegian support can be arranged.
